title.value: Relationship Between Arterial Stiffness Index, Pulse Pressure, and Magnetic Resonance Imaging Markers of White Matter Integrity: A UK Biobank Study
title.justification: The title indicates the focus on the relationship between arterial stiffness, pulse pressure, and brain integrity. It reflects the paper's investigation aim and the population study used (UK Biobank).
title.quote: Relationship Between Arterial Stiffness Index, Pulse Pressure, and Magnetic Resonance Imaging Markers of White Matter Integrity: A UK Biobank Study

extractions.description: This paper investigates the association between peripheral pulse pressure (PP), arterial stiffness index (ASI), and brain integrity using data from 17,984 participants of the UK Biobank. The study finds that peripheral PP is a better predictor of white matter integrity when compared to ASI. These results are consistent until the age of 75, beyond which no significant relationship is found.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The primary focus of the paper is on the health parameters associated with aging and their effects on brain integrity, which does not centrally relate to climate or ecological sustainable development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Alzheimer’s disease and dementia in general constitute one of the major public health problems of the 21st century.

primary_category.justification: The paper primarily explores health aspects related to aging and arterial stiffness rather than focusing on themes of climate or ecological sustainable development.
primary_category.quote: The aim of the study is to investigate the association between peripheral PP, arterial stiffness index (ASI) and brain integrity, and to discover if ASI is a better predictor of white matter integrity than peripheral PP.

secondary_categories.justification: The themes discussed in the paper do not align with the secondary climate or ecological sustainable development categories.
secondary_categories.quote: This study included 17,984 participants, mean age 63.09 ± 7.31 years, of which 9,311 are female.

primary_sub_category.justification: There is no sub-category within climate or ecological sustainable development that aligns with the study's focus on health parameters and neurological outcomes.
primary_sub_category.quote: Results: An important finding is that peripheral PP better predicts white matter integrity when compared to ASI.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: No sub-category from the climate or ecological sustainable development list pertains to the paper's subject matter.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: These results suggest that ASI from plethysmography should not be used to estimate cerebrovascular integrity in older adults.

applications.justification: The study does not discuss applications related to climate or ecological sustainable development; it focuses on predictive health metrics for neurological aging.
applications.quote: To test the hypothesis that ASI is a better predictor of white matter integrity than peripheral PP, a stepwise linear model was performed.

new_primary_category.justification: The existing categories related to climate and ecological sustainability do not fit the subject matter of this research paper, which is largely health-focused.
new_primary_category.quote: This paper was submitted to Neurocognitive Aging and Behavior, a section of the journal Frontiers in Aging Neuroscience.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The research does not align with new categories related to climate or ecological sustainability due to its focus on neurological health characteristics rather than environmental factors.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: Conclusion: These results suggest that ASI from plethysmography should not be used to estimate cerebrovascular integrity in older adults and further question the relationship between arterial stiffness, blood pressure, and white matter damage after the age of 75 years old.
